head: 666f197ee1be38edc4d28a8b94212fc49de4be55
summary:
Criteria 1 to 4 hold on this machine, checked by commands run here rather than read from earlier stages.
- The rename is live in StallRig. I built StallRig from its csproj, outside FsAnalyser.slnx, into a scratch folder: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Reflection on the built StallRig.dll shows RigLock has exactly one constant, SessionName = `Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig`. No `MachineName` identifier is left anywhere in code.
- The kernel object is unchanged (O-005). The shell held `[Threading.Mutex]::new($false,'Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig')` (createdNew=True). The built StallRig.exe --wait-sec 2 then exited 1 after 2314 ms, with a TimeoutException that names `Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig`. There were 0 127.0.0.1 mappings before and after.
- The three comments are corrected, and WindowCases.ps1 parses with 0 errors under both PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444 and 7.6.6. It has no BOM and 0 bytes >= 0x80, the same as its parent. Its diff is one line.
- The full default suite passes 373/373. The 21 targeted tests pass: 18 SmbRigTests, 2 parse cases, 1 wording test.
- The checks catch a regression. Reverting StalledShareTests.cs:17 made RigLockScopeWordingTests fail, naming that line. Putting back the parent commit's three files made Fitness report 4 violations, at Program.cs:13, StalledShareTests.cs:17, and WindowCases.ps1:1333 twice. After restoring them (hashes identical), Fitness reports that all 59 rules hold.

Three things keep this from a full pass:
- O-006 is owed to this stage and I could not discharge it. Whether one sign-in session's SMB mappings are invisible to another needs a second logon session. The spike showed this sandbox cannot create one, and neither of the elevated operations would create one.
- Criterion 5 (cross-session exclusion) was deliberately not built. The design marks it non-material. The doc now states the limit and the trigger for a future switch to `Global\`. But whether `Local\` fails to span sessions, and whether `Global\` would span them, is still not measured.
- O-007, which code-review assigned to build-slice, is still open in the tree. I re-measured its premise: 5.1 parses non-ASCII in a comment with 0 errors and in a string with 2. So WindowScriptParseTests cannot catch the comment case its summary claims, and no test guards the file's ASCII-only invariant.

This is not a loop: build-slice ran once, with no caused_by.

checks.what: Repo-local .NET 10 SDK, session and integrity of this shell
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 --version; (Get-Process -Id $PID).SessionId; whoami /groups | Select-String 'Mandatory Level'

checks.what: No MachineName identifier left; every consumer of the lock string
checks.command: Grep MachineName|SessionName|FsAnalyser-SmbRig over the tree excluding .taad/
checks.evidence: Code has only SmbRig.cs:176 `public const string SessionName = @"Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig"` and SmbRig.cs:51 `RigLock.Take(RigLock.SessionName, ...)`, plus the cref at SmbRigTests.cs:8. The one `MachineName` left is the historical sentence at docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:243, which describes SL-038 build 2 and is accurate as history. SmbRigTests.cs:137 uses GUID-suffixed test names. WindowCases.ps1 never opens this mutex by string: its own are FsAnalyser-WindowCases-*. It matches StallRig's message text 'Another stall-rig run' at :1353, which is unchanged.

checks.what: StallRig builds outside FsAnalyser.slnx after the rename
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build tests/window/StallRig/StallRig.csproj -c Release -o %TEMP%\sl059-validate-stallrig
checks.evidence: Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s), exit 0. The build was incremental (1.14 s), so the output was checked by reflection in the next check.

checks.what: The built StallRig.dll carries the renamed constant with the unchanged value
checks.evidence: SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig (the only static field), runtime 10.0.12

checks.what: Real contention: the built StallRig.exe opens the same kernel object that PowerShell opens by string (O-005)
checks.command: $m=[Threading.Mutex]::new($false,'Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig',[ref]$created); $m.WaitOne(0); then StallRig.exe --marker <temp>\armed.txt --wait-sec 2 with stdin closed; count-only Get-SmbMapping filtered to \\127.0.0.1\* before and after
checks.evidence: holder: createdNew=True held=True session=1. StallRig: exit=1 after 2314 ms, stdout empty, stderr 'StallRig: TimeoutException: Another stall-rig run held Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig for 2 s, so this run did not start. Two rig runs cannot share 127.0.0.1: the SMB client allows one port per server name.' 127.0.0.1 mappings before=0, after=0. The temp run folder, including the tree StallRig leaves on a lock timeout, was deleted.

checks.what: In one session, a Local\ name and a Global\ name with the same suffix are separate objects
checks.command: hold Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig-sl059probe here; in a second pwsh process open the Local\ name, then the Global\ name with the same suffix
checks.evidence: Other process: Local\ createdNew=False, WaitOne(0)=False. Global\ createdNew=True, WaitOne(0)=True. Session 1 only; this says nothing about behaviour across sessions.
Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 373, Skipped: 0, Total: 373, Duration: 22 s, exit 0

checks.what: Targeted tests by name: 18 SmbRigTests, both WindowScriptParseTests hosts, and RigLockScopeWordingTests
checks.evidence: Total tests: 21, all passed: ASecondRunWaitsForTheFirst, ALiveHolderFailsTheNextRunLoudlyAndAKilledOneDoesNotBlockIt, 16 OnlyTheRigsOwnMappingsAreSwept cases, WindowCasesParses(powershell.exe, Desktop), WindowCasesParses(pwsh.exe, Core), NothingSaysTheRigLockSpansTheMachine

checks.what: WindowCases.ps1 parses under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7
WindowCases.ps1 encoding kept: no BOM, pure ASCII, one-line diff
checks.command: [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes on the working file and on git show 2d47315c0:tests/window/WindowCases.ps1; git diff --numstat 2d47315c0 HEAD
checks.evidence: Working file: bom=False, nonascii=0. Parent: bom=False, nonascii=0. numstat 1/1. The byte counts differ only by CRLF (checkout) versus LF (git show).

checks.what: Mutation: the wording test fails when a stale comment comes back
checks.command: Replace 'in this sign-in session.' with 'on this machine.' in StalledShareTests.cs, run the RigLockScopeWordingTests filter --no-build, then git checkout
checks.evidence: Failed! 1 failed, and the failure names tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/StalledShareTests.cs:17. The mutant exited 1. The file was restored with the same hash.

checks.what: Fitness: the declared rules hold on the tree, and fire when the three parent-commit files are put back
checks.command: Fitness op=check (rebuild) on the tree; git checkout 2d47315c0 -- the three files; Fitness check; git checkout HEAD -- the three files; Fitness check
checks.evidence: Tree: 59 rules, every declared rule holds. With the parent files: 4 violations, at StalledShareTests.cs:17, WindowCases.ps1:1333 (both patterns) and StallRig/Program.cs:13. Restored: hashes identical, 59 rules hold, and git status shows only the engine's .taad records.

checks.what: Residual machine-wide claims about RigLock: read each grep hit
checks.command: Grep -i 'machine-wide|on this machine|MachineName' over tests, docs, eng, src; Grep -i 'system-wide|all sessions|every session|across sessions|whole machine|per machine'
checks.evidence: Remaining hits, none of which claims RigLock is machine-wide: SL-020-scanner.md:32 (DFS, not measured), SL-020-scanner.md:243 (history of the SL-038 rename), eng/dotnet.ps1:5 (SDK), WindowCases.ps1:1985 and 2118 (measurements), TempTree.cs:150 (Developer Mode), and the wording test quoting itself. All were left unedited. The second grep hit only the wording test.

checks.what: Premise of O-007 re-measured: 5.1 accepts non-ASCII in a comment but not in a string
checks.command: UTF-8 no-BOM scratch scripts in %TEMP% with an em dash and curly quotes: one in a comment, one in a double-quoted string; powershell.exe ParseFile
checks.evidence: 5.1 comment errors=0; 5.1 string errors=2. So WindowScriptParseTests cannot catch the comment case its summary claims (WindowScriptParseTests.cs:8-9). The scratch folder was deleted.

checks.what: O-007 fix present in the tree
checks.evidence: The summary still says it catches 'a non-ASCII dash or quote in an edited comment'. There is no byte >= 0x80 or BOM assertion. The tree is unchanged since 666f197. O-007 is owed to build-slice.

checks.what: O-006: are SMB mappings from one sign-in session invisible to the rig's sweep in another?
checks.evidence: Needs a second logon session. Spike 1 recorded the sandbox refusing Register-ScheduledTask (S4U). runas and self-elevation are forbidden. Neither registered elevated operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) creates a session or reads SMB mappings.

checks.what: Cross-session mutual exclusion under Local\ or Global\ (criterion 5)
checks.evidence: No second sign-in session is reachable (same reason as O-006). The design marks the case non-material and deferred. Spike 2 cases (a), (b) and (c) never ran.

checks.what: Person-run network pass (WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork; Core.Tests with Network=SMB-LOOPBACK)
checks.evidence: Opt-in. It changes this machine's SMB client mappings and is run by a person, not by an engine stage. StallRig was run only as far as the lock timeout, before any mapping step.

criteria.criterion: 1. Rename RigLock's public scope constant, including when StallRig is built outside FsAnalyser.slnx
criteria.how: StallRig built from its csproj outside the slnx: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Reflection on the built StallRig.dll shows RigLock.SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig as its only static field. No MachineName identifier in code. The built exe contends with a PowerShell holder of the same string (exit 1, TimeoutException naming the lock).

criteria.criterion: 2. Correct the stale 'on this machine' comments, with WindowCases.ps1 still parsing under Windows PowerShell 5.1
criteria.how: The diff shows the three comments now say 'in this sign-in session' or 'per sign-in session'. ParseFile gives 0 errors under 5.1.26100.9444 and 7.6.6. No BOM, 0 non-ASCII bytes (same as the parent), numstat 1/1. The suite's parse test alone would not catch a non-ASCII comment (see O-007); the byte check here was run directly.

criteria.criterion: 3. Sweep for residual machine-wide claims about RigLock, leaving unrelated hits alone
criteria.how: Read every grep hit: none claims RigLock is machine-wide, and the unrelated hits (SDK, measurements, Developer Mode, DFS, the history sentence) are unedited. RigLockScopeWordingTests passes, and fails naming StalledShareTests.cs:17 when that comment is reverted. Fitness: 0 violations on the tree, 4 with the parent's files.

criteria.criterion: 4. RigLock's existing in-session serialisation, covered by the 18 existing SmbRigTests
criteria.how: 18/18 SmbRigTests pass by name. The real built StallRig.exe also fails loudly (exit 1 in 2314 ms, lock named) while another process in session 1 holds Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig. Full suite 373/373.

criteria.criterion: 5. Cross-session mutual exclusion of RigLock, when two processes in different sign-in sessions both hold a Global\ named mutex
criteria.how: The design's handling is there: there is no Global\ anywhere, and SL-020-scanner.md:255-262 says runs from different sessions are NOT serialised and gives the trigger (switch to Global\ and prove it in both orders, with a person running it). The behaviour itself was never measured: no second session is reachable from here.

planned.evidence: StallRig csproj built outside the slnx with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Reflection on StallRig.dll: SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig. Grep finds no MachineName identifier in code. The live exe contends on the same kernel object.
The three comment lines are changed. WindowCases.ps1 ParseFile gives 0 errors under 5.1 and 7.6.6, no BOM, 0 bytes >= 0x80, and a one-line diff.

I read every grep hit for machine-wide, on this machine and MachineName over tests, docs, eng and src; the unrelated hits are unedited. Wording test mutation fails at StalledShareTests.cs:17. Fitness: 0 violations on the tree, 4 on the parent's files.
18/18 SmbRigTests pass by name (2 lock tests plus 16 sweep cases). Full suite 373/373. The real StallRig.exe times out loudly against a held Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig.

Deferred by the design (material:false), and the doc states the limit and the trigger. Cross-session behaviour is unmeasured: spike 1 showed the sandbox cannot create a second session, and no registered elevated operation creates one.

obligations.evidence: Grep: the only code references are SmbRig.cs:51 and :176 (SessionName) and the cref at SmbRigTests.cs:8. MachineName survives only in the historical doc sentence at SL-020-scanner.md:243. StallRig was built outside the slnx (0/0), and reflection on its dll gives SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig. Live: this shell held [Threading.Mutex]::new($false,'Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig') (createdNew=True), and the built StallRig.exe --wait-sec 2 exited 1 after 2314 ms with 'Another stall-rig run held Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig for 2 s'. WindowCases.ps1 does not open this mutex by string; it checks StallRig's unchanged message text (:1353).

Not measurable from this run. It needs a second logon or sign-in session with an SMB mapping made in one and Get-SmbMapping read in the other. Spike 1 recorded the sandbox vetoing Register-ScheduledTask (S4U). runas and self-elevation are forbidden. The registered elevated operations (whoami, read-denied-folders) create no session and read no mappings, so asking for one would not settle it. A person has to run it.

Owed to build-slice and still open in the tree. WindowScriptParseTests.cs:8-9 still claims it catches a non-ASCII dash or quote in an edited comment, and there is no byte >= 0x80 or BOM assertion. Premise re-measured: 5.1 ParseFile gives 0 errors on non-ASCII in a comment and 2 in a string. The file itself is ASCII today (0 bytes >= 0x80), but nothing in the suite keeps it that way.

not_reached: O-006: whether an SMB mapping made in one sign-in session is visible to Get-SmbMapping, and so to the rig's sweep, in another. That needs a second session, which a person has to create (Fast User Switching, or an S4U task registered by hand).

Cross-session behaviour of the lock itself. The doc now states that Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig is not seen from another session, and that Global\ would be. Both come from recalled Microsoft semantics; spike 2 cases (a), (b) and (c) never ran.

Whether the SMB client's 'one port per server name' limit for 127.0.0.1 applies per logon session or across the whole machine. If it is machine-wide, two rig runs in different sessions could still clash at the redirector even though the lock does not serialise them. The doc names the lock's scope but not this.

The person-run network pass (WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork, then Core.Tests with Network=SMB-LOOPBACK) at this HEAD. StallRig was run only as far as the lock timeout, never through a real mapping.
A machine without pwsh.exe on PATH: the default suite now launches pwsh.exe (WindowScriptParseTests), which is present here (7.6.6) but not guaranteed elsewhere.
